content:
maya: Heads up — rack-23 (r23-n[12-15]) started showing a rise in tail latency and 30–40% throughput loss around 03:12 UTC. Node telemetry shows repeated NVLink link flaps + PCIe AER non-fatal resets. Impacting some Dedicated pools.

alex: Can you paste the kernel dmesg slice + nvidia logs? rough timeline is enough.

maya: Pasting the relevant bits:
```
Mar 08 03:11:58 r23-n14 kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error: severity=Uncorrected
Mar 08 03:11:58 r23-n14 kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: device [10de:1db6] error status/mask = 0x00000001/0x00002000
Mar 08 03:12:01 r23-n14 kernel: nvlink: link 0->1 status change: L0->L1
Mar 08 03:12:01 r23-n14 kernel: nvlink: link 0->1 flap detected, count=6
Mar 08 03:12:03 r23-n14 kernel: nvidia: Xid (PCIe AER) 43 detected on GPU 2
```

jordan: Xid 43 is a typical PCIe/aer-induced GPU hw error (non-deterministic). Any ECC correctable spikes?

maya: ECC correctable spikes correlate — see `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` snippet: `GPU2 ECC_C 120 -> 430 in 5m` (CTR surge).

eli: This looks like a flaky card or riser/backplane. Recommend we drain the impacted nodes and isolate the card. If it's Dedicated, customers will feel the SLO hit.

alex: Agreed. Steps: 1) cordon + drain the nodes, 2) capture full lspci/aer counters, 3) collect kernel + nv-hostengine logs, 4) try reseat & BIOS PCIe link speed fallback (Gen3->Gen2) if reseat reproduces.

maya: I'm starting eviction now for r23-n12..n15 (cordon+drain). K8s commands used: `kubectl cordon r23-n14 && kubectl drain r23-n14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

sre_bot: [alert] perf-deg: rack-23 GPU throughput drop 35% — affected pools: dedicated-a, hosted-b — incident id INC-2026-311.

jordan: Before RMA, can you run `lspci -vvv -s 65:00.0` and `cat /sys/kernel/debug/pcie_aer/65:00.0` and attach outputs? Also run `nvmlDeviceGetRetiredPages` (via nvidia-smi) to confirm HW retirements.

maya: Uploading artifacts to /tmp/r23-n14-triage.tar.gz (logs + lspci + nv-hostengine). Link: https://internal-storage/reports/r23-n14-triage.tar.gz

eli: If reseating doesn't reduce flap rate, we should swap the card to spare slot in same node and run burn-in 30m. If the behavior follows the card -> RMA. If it stays on slot -> backplane/riser issue.

alex: Also check firmware: BIOS microcode on r23 hosts is 1.5.2 but some older risers need BIOS 1.5.3 to avoid link renegotiation bugs. Any recent BIOS updates this week?

maya: No BIOS changes in last month. Host firmware is stable. We do have a few recent PCIe AER counter resets after noisy power cycling during maintenance last week.

sre_lead: TL;DR operational plan: 1) drain nodes (in progress), 2) reseat card in r23-n14, run 30m stress (tensor-bench 2x), 3) if still flapping -> swap to spare in r23-n21, 4) open RMA with vendor, mark card as suspect, 5) schedule backfill for Dedicated pools (we'll spin up temporary nodes in eu-west-1 to avoid SLO violations).

jordan: One more callout — NVLink flaps often show up with mixed gen topologies or mismatched NV driver/firmware combos. Confirmed driver is 535.98 and NVLink fw is 48.07 (from host manifest).

eli: Cost impact note: spinning temporary nodes in eu-west-1 for Dedicated backfill will cost ~ $2.6k/week at current commit levels; CT will need to sign off if we exceed monthly variance.

alex: For diagnostics, enable pcie_aer debug counters for 10m: `echo 1 > /sys/module/pcie_aer/parameters/enable` (careful — noisy). Also capture `pcie_aspm_errors` if present.

maya: Reseat done on GPU2 -> initial 20m run looks cleaner (no flaps in first 18m). But not confident — keeping node drained for now. Repeating stress for 1h.

sre_bot: [update] node r23-n14 drained, workloads rescheduled.

jordan: Good. If the hour run passes, we can put back into rotation and monitor with a stricter alert (3 flaps in 30m -> auto-drain).

sre_lead: If flaps return after reseat, treat as RMA. Please mark the card with tag: suspect-aer-0311 and attach the triage bundle to the RMA ticket.

maya: Noted. I'll keep this thread updated with the stress results and attach the lspci / aer dumps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks — let's converge by EOD UTC. If anyone oncall needs to take over, ping @sre_lead.
